text:
Compelled by miserable cynicism,

Judas is there at that supper,

and though he restrains envy and fear,

he lowers his bewildered eyes.


Christ, withdrawn into his dreams,

and with a word full of sweetness,

without anger says, in serene calm:

"One who is here has betrayed me!"


Then the apostles trembled;

looking at one another in fear, they wavered...

and Peter, rising, cried:


"Say which of us is guilty,

so I may spit in the wretch's face!"

And Christ said nothing. He smiled.

translation.title: The Last Hour
translation.editorial_note: The translation keeps the sonnet's dramatic contrast between Peter's fury and Christ's silent smile.
